analysis: Integration of 5 units. The PR changes release-note derivation only: scripts/provider-release-publication.py release_changelog (head ~lines 56-68) now runs `git tag --list --format=%(contents)%00%(contents:signature)%00 -- <tag>` with a list-argument subprocess and no shell, so the tag name and annotation stay data. Output is parsed as bytes: split on NUL, removesuffix(signature), UTF-8 decode, strip. Only `contents` and `signature` are parsed. A NUL in the annotation or a non-UTF-8 annotation would raise ValueError/UnicodeDecodeError, which fails closed at prepare time. This is a CI availability edge case, not a trust bypass, and git does not accept NULs in tag messages. The changelog goes only into the registration payload and the retained release-payload.json. That payload stays digest-bound via RELEASE_PAYLOAD_SHA256 and RELEASE_PROVENANCE_SHA256 and is re-checked by checked_payload. The changelog is not an identity field for build qualification (A-011/A-017, T-054). Tag authenticity remains covered by the existing signed-tag/verify_tag gates, which are not touched in the supplied diff. The new tests (scripts/test-provider-release-publication.py 18-70 and 274-305) use isolated temp repos with no global config, hooks or signing, and fake armor. They assert that payload fields other than changelog, the bundle and the provenance are unchanged, and that tampering fails with a digest mismatch, which reinforces the immutability controls. The docs (docs/operations/provider-release.md ~149 and 463, docs/developer/test.md ~837) match the code. No change to the provider runtime, the coordinator WebSocket contract, key custody, attestation, App Attest authorization, the prefix cache (T-041) or the fan helper. Limits: integration_source was incomplete (14 units omitted), so unchanged callers of release_changelog and how the notes are rendered downstream were not examined. The 64 KiB registration body limit is enforced outside the supplied evidence. No finding qualifies.
